tagline: Three mountain roads connect desert valleys with pine and fir forests
intro: Lee Canyon, Deer Creek and Kyle Canyon roads connect a drive through the Spring Mountains northwest of Las Vegas. Lee Canyon and Deer Creek roads are Nevada Scenic Byways, along with the westernmost 13 miles of Kyle Canyon Road. The Forest Service describes a landscape rising from creosote bush and Mojave yucca to ponderosa pine, white fir and high ridges of bristlecone pine. Kyle Canyon Road loses 3,000 feet in 20 miles on its descent toward Las Vegas. Towering cliffs, steep hillsides and deep, narrow canyons separate the mountain country from the surrounding desert.

Both canyon roads began as county routes documented by 1933. Kyle Canyon Road was fully paved and numbered SR 39 by 1935. Lee Canyon Road shifted to its present alignment by 1937; its section between U.S. 95 and the forest was paved by 1940. The Nevada Department of Transportation gave both canyon roads scenic designations in July 1998.

Start on Lee Canyon Road from U.S. 95 and travel toward the canyon’s community and recreation area. Deer Creek Road links Lee Canyon with Kyle Canyon Road east of Mount Charleston. Continue down Kyle Canyon past the Spring Mountains Visitor Gateway, where public trails and exhibits occupy reclaimed golf-course land. Farther east, Kyle Canyon Road returns to U.S. 95.
notice: Ponderosa pine and white fir cover lower mountain slopes; bristlecone pine grows on higher ridges and slopes.

moments.title: Lee Canyon
moments.text: Lee Canyon combines a small community with a mountain recreation area reached by Lee Canyon Road. At McWilliams Campground, ponderosa and white pines surround more than 70 campsites. Nearby, the Lower Bristlecone Trailhead provides access to the Bristlecone Trail. Old Mill is a seasonal day-use picnic area with 80 individual sites.

moments.title: Deer Creek picnic area
moments.text: About halfway along Deer Creek Highway, the picnic area places its parking lot and restroom on one side of the road and the trail to picnic sites on the other. This is the connecting road between Lee and Kyle canyons. Mahogany Grove, also on Deer Creek Highway, lies near remnants of a Civilian Conservation Corps campground developed in the 1930s.

moments.title: Spring Mountains Visitor Gateway
moments.text: Seven Stones Plaza honors the Nuwuvi relationship with the Spring Mountains. The Nuwuvi consider these mountains the place of creation, and tribal members continue to visit and honor them. The plaza is part of a 128-acre complex reclaimed from a golf course for trails, exhibits and public buildings. The Silent Heroes of the Cold War National Memorial also honors 14 people killed in a 1955 flight that crashed on Charleston Peak. A telescope on the Pack Rat Trail provides a view of the crash site. The memorial includes a propeller recovered from the aircraft and a granite monument.
